concepts.text: Demand for Constituent Assembly (1934-1946)
children: First proposal for a Constituent Assembly in 1934 by M.N. Roy
Official demand by Indian National Congress in 1935
Jawaharlal Nehru's declaration in 1938 that the Constitution of free India be framed by a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise
British acceptance of demand in principle through the August Offer of 1940
Cripps Proposals of 1942: British draft for framing independent Constitution after World War II
Muslim League's rejection of Cripps Proposals and demand for two separate Constituent Assemblies
Cabinet Mission (members: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander; arrived March 24, 1946; published plan May 16, 1946)
Cabinet Mission's rejection of the idea of two Constituent Assemblies
Cabinet Mission's scheme for a Constituent Assembly (partly elected, partly nominated)
Satisfaction of Muslim League with the Cabinet Mission scheme

concepts.text: Composition and Election of Constituent Assembly
children: Total strength: 389 (296 from British Indian provinces, 93 from princely states, 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces)
Allocation of seats in proportion to population, roughly one seat per million, divided among Muslims, Sikhs, and General
Members elected indirectly by provincial legislative assembly members using proportional representation by single transferable vote; princely state representatives nominated by their heads
Limited franchise for provincial elections under Government of India Act 1935 (based on tax, property, education)
Elections held in July-August 1946: Congress won 208 seats, Muslim League 73, others 15
Community-wise representation in the Assembly: Hindus 163, Muslims 80, Scheduled Castes 31, Indian Christians 6, Backward Tribes 6, Sikhs 4, Anglo-Indians 3, Parsees 3
Princely states initially stayed away; six states (Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa, Udaipur) joined on April 28, 1947
After partition: Muslim League members from Pakistan areas withdrew; total strength reduced to 299 (provinces 229, states 70)

concepts.text: First Meeting and Officers of Constituent Assembly
children: First meeting held on December 9, 1946; Muslim League boycotted; 211 members attended
Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha served as temporary President following French practice of electing the oldest member
Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected as President of the Assembly
H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari elected as Vice-Presidents

concepts.text: Objectives Resolution
children: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946
Unanimously adopted on January 22, 1947
Proclaimed India as an Independent Sovereign Republic
Declared India as a Union of territories comprising British India, Indian States, and other willing parts
Provided for autonomous units with residuary powers
Stated that all power and authority are derived from the people
Guaranteed justice – social, economic and political
Guaranteed equality of status, opportunity and before the law
Guaranteed freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship, vocation, association and action subject to law and public morality
Provided safeguards for minorities, backward and tribal areas, depressed and other backward classes
Affirmed integrity of territory and sovereign rights on land, sea and air
Declared India's rightful and honoured place in the world and contribution to world peace and welfare of mankind
Influenced the entire Constitution; its modified version forms the Preamble

concepts.text: Post-Partition Changes and Finalization
children: Mountbatten Plan of June 3, 1947 led to partition
After the Plan, representatives of most princely states joined the Assembly
Members of Muslim League from areas within Indian Dominion entered the Assembly
Indian Independence Act of 1947 made three changes: (i) Assembly became fully sovereign, (ii) empowered to abrogate or alter any British law, (iii) became a legislative body with separate functions
Assembly performed two functions: Constituent body chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Legislative body chaired by G.V. Mavlankar
Muslim League members from areas included in Pakistan withdrew; total strength reduced to 299
India's membership of the Commonwealth ratified in May 1949
National flag adopted on July 22, 1947; national anthem and national song adopted on January 24, 1950
Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected as first President of India on January 24, 1950
Constituent Assembly continued as Provisional Parliament from January 26, 1950 to April 17, 1952
First elected Parliament with two Houses came in May 1952; first general elections held in 1951-52

concepts.text: Drafting Committee
children: Set up on August 29, 1947
Most important committee of the Constituent Assembly
Task: to prepare a draft of the new Constitution

Seven members: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau (replaced B.L. Mitter), T.T. Krishnamachari (replaced D.P. Khaitan)
First draft published in February 1948; eight months given for public discussion
Second draft published in October 1948
Final draft introduced by Dr. Ambedkar on November 4, 1948 (first reading)
Three readings: general discussion (Nov 4-9, 1948), clause-by-clause consideration (Nov 15, 1948 to Oct 17, 1949), final reading (Nov 14-26, 1949)
7,653 amendments proposed; 2,473 discussed
Motion to pass Constitution moved by Dr. Ambedkar on November 14, 1949; passed on November 26, 1949
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar piloted the Draft Constitution as Law Minister; known as Father of the Constitution

concepts.text: Criticism of Constituent Assembly
children: Assembly not truly representative: members were not directly elected on universal adult franchise
Assembly not sovereign: created and sessions held with permission of British Government
Process time-consuming: American Constitution framed in 4 months; Naziruddin Ahmed called Drafting Committee 'Drifting Committee'
Assembly dominated by Congress party: Granville Austin remarked 'The Assembly was the Congress and the Congress was India'
Assembly dominated by lawyers and politicians: other sections not sufficiently represented; resulting in bulky and complicated language
Assembly dominated by Hindus: Lord Viscount Simon called it 'a body of Hindus'; Winston Churchill said it represented 'only one major community'

concepts.text: Major Committees of Constituent Assembly
children: Union Powers Committee – Chairman Jawaharlal Nehru
Union Constitution Committee – Chairman Jawaharlal Nehru
Provincial Constitution Committee – Chairman Sardar Patel
Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas – Chairman Sardar Patel
Rules of Procedure Committee – Chairman Dr. Rajendra Prasad
States Committee (Committee for Negotiating with States) – Chairman Jawaharlal Nehru
Steering Committee – Chairman Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Finance and Staff Committee – Chairman Dr. Rajendra Prasad

concepts.text: Experts Committee (July 1946)
children: Appointed on July 8, 1946 to prepare material for the Constituent Assembly
Members: Jawaharlal Nehru (Chairman), M. Asaf Ali, K.M. Munshi, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.T. Shah, D.R. Gadgil, Humayun Kabir, K. Santhanam; Krishna Kripalani co-opted as member and convener
First sitting in New Delhi (July 20-22, 1946); second sitting in Bombay (Aug 15-17, 1946)
Discussed procedure, appointment of committees, and drafted a resolution on objectives (later Objectives Resolution)
Granville Austin noted its role in setting India on the road to the present Constitution

concepts.text: Functionaries and Artistic Aspects of the Constitution
children: Sir B.N. Rau appointed as Constitutional Advisor (legal advisor) to the Constituent Assembly
H.V.R. Iyengar as Secretary to the Constituent Assembly
S.N. Mukerjee as Chief Draftsman
Prem Behari Narain Raizada as calligrapher who handwrote the original Constitution in flowing italic style
Artists from Shantiniketan (Nand Lal Bose, Beohar Rammanohar Sinha) beautified and decorated the original version
Hindi version calligraphy by Vasant Krishan Vaidya and decoration by Nand Lal Bose
Originally no authoritative text in Hindi; 58th Constitutional Amendment Act (1987) inserted Article 394-A providing for an authoritative Hindi text
Article 394-A: President to cause publication of Hindi translation, modifications for conformity, inclusion of amendments, same meaning as English, and provision for revision if difficulty arises

concepts.text: Commencement of Constitution and Republic Day
children: Some provisions (specified articles like 5,6,7,8,9,60,324, etc.) came into force on November 26, 1949
Remaining provisions came into force on January 26, 1950 – the date of commencement
January 26 chosen due to historical significance: Purna Swaraj day celebrated on January 26, 1930 following Lahore Session of INC (December 1929)
Indian Independence Act 1947 and Government of India Act 1935, along with all amending enactments, were repealed
Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act (1949) was continued
Part XXII originally contained Articles 393 (Short title), 394 (Commencement), 395 (Repeals); Article 394A added by 58th Amendment

concepts.text: Elephant adopted as symbol (seal) of the Constituent Assembly
Total duration taken to frame the Constitution: 2 years, 11 months and 18 days
Total expenditure on framing the Constitution: ₹64 lakh
Constitution-makers studied the constitutions of about 60 countries
Draft Constitution considered by the Assembly for 114 days
The Constituent Assembly held 11 sessions from December 1946 to November 1949, with a final meeting for signatures on January 24, 1950
Original Constitution adopted contained a Preamble, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules
284 out of 299 members signed the Constitution on November 26, 1949
The Preamble was enacted after the entire Constitution was enacted
